name: Royal Forth Yacht Club
desc: Visitor berth candidate. FTNS can send a leisure yacht here instead of a commercial Forth Ports dock — confirm availability with the harbour or club first.
body:
The senior club at Granton. Home of the Scottish Dragon fleet, with racing most Saturdays, some Sundays and two weekday evenings each fortnight from April to October.

Hosts the Edinburgh Regatta with Forth Corinthian YC and the One Design Regatta (typically mid-September). Cadets and open sailing evenings run through the season. Lift-in is usually mid-April; the pillar crane runs to the end of October.

Waters used: Cramond, Inchmickery, Inchcolm to the west of Granton, and Inchkeith to the east. Not a navigation product — club sailing instructions govern courses.

Visitor berth: Granton is the right Edinburgh answer for a sailing yacht arriving from the Continent — not Leith and not Grangemouth. Contact the club / Edinburgh Marina pontoon before sending them in.
facts:
Season ~ April – October
Evenings ~ Wed / Thu series
Weekend ~ Saturday series + opens
Facilities ~ Moorings, Crane, pontoon

name: Forth Corinthian Yacht Club
desc: Visitor berth candidate. FTNS can send a leisure yacht here instead of a commercial Forth Ports dock — confirm availability with the harbour or club first.
body:
Shares Granton Harbour with the Royal Forth. Joint host of the Edinburgh Regatta. Local racing uses the same Granton waters — Cramond, Inchmickery, Inchcolm and Inchkeith — with longer passage races toward Anstruther, Dunbar and Eyemouth.

A Forth Yacht Clubs Association member. Good partner for the working group on inter-club calendar clashes and visitor berthing at Granton.
facts:
Base ~ Granton, with RFYC
Open event ~ Edinburgh Regatta (joint)

name: Port Edgar Yacht Club
desc: Visitor berth candidate. FTNS can send a leisure yacht here instead of a commercial Forth Ports dock — confirm availability with the harbour or club first.
body:
The club under the Forth Bridges. Yacht and dinghy racing from Port Edgar Marina, with twilight handicap racing midweek and weekend series. The club owns keelboats used for mentored racing.

National-scale events come here: 707 Sprints (early October 2026) and previous 707 Nationals. RYA Scotland has also used the venue for the Celtic Cup youth event. Dinghy courses are run from the pier race box or a committee boat in Queensferry Bay — sea state on the north-side marks can be ugly in wind-over-tide.

This is the natural pin for anything that has to live with commercial and cruise traffic under the bridges.

Visitor berth: Port Edgar Marina is the first place FTNS should name when a leisure yacht asks for a night under the bridges. Rosyth next door is not the substitute.
facts:
Season ~ Almost Daily Apr - Aug
Evenings ~ Twilight series
Open ~ 707 sprints / Nationals
Marina ~ Port Edgar Marina

name: East Lothian Yacht Club
desc: Visitor berth candidate. FTNS can send a leisure yacht here instead of a commercial Forth Ports dock — confirm availability with the harbour or club first.
body:
The principal East Lothian club, racing off North Berwick with Bass Rock as the backdrop. Strong dinghy and keelboat programmes, a published mark chart, and a history of hosting class nationals (RS, Solo, Musto Skiff and others).

The annual open regatta and the keelboat regatta pull visiting boats from across Scotland. White-sail autumn series runs into September. This pin is how a visiting fleet should first read North Berwick — not only as a fishing harbour.
facts:
Open ~ ELYC Regatta + Keelboat Regatta
Classes ~ ILCA, Aero, RS, Skiff, white sail
Marks ~ Published racing marks

name: Dalgety Bay Sailing Club
body: Dinghy club on the Fife shore at Dalgety Bay, immediately east of the bridges. Members appear in Forth open fleets (including Scottish Skiffs at ELYC). A useful north-shore voice for the working group — different tide, different fetch, different commercial neighbours from Granton or Port Edgar.
facts:
Water ~ North Forth, east of the bridges
Note ~ Active in Forth open events
